answer: Agents resist Sybil attacks by locking exclusive serial time on a glacier-mounted hollow-core sampler that extracts a unique ice-ocean interface core. The sampler’s non-exportable hardware key signs the live density and salinity profile, which the panel verifies against public satellite altimetry and buoy streams. Because only one identity can operate the physical sampler at a time and cores cannot be cloned or shared, an attacker must source, transport, and schedule distinct instruments; logistics and scarcity make the cost grow super-linearly and non-amortizable across identities.
